meta.title: Decently and in Order
meta.sub: A course in Presbyterian church government, worked through the Book of Church Order of the Presbyterian Church in America
meta.edition: Checked against the 2026 edition of the Book of Church Order, published by the Office of the Stated Clerk, which carries every amendment through the 53rd General Assembly (Louisville, Kentucky, June 22–26, 2026).

units.d: Where church government comes from, the three answers churches give, and how this one took shape.
A walk through the canon: a people taught and judged, a Shepherd who rules, and churches learning to decide.
The eight principles in front of the book, what the Constitution is, how far church power reaches, and what officers vow.
The visible church, the particular church, and the people on its rolls.
Elders and deacons: calling, qualification, election, ordination.
Session, presbytery and Assembly, and the commissions they appoint.
How a church court actually does business, and what protects the minority in it.
From a man under care to an installed pastor.
Meetings, property, withdrawal, and the planting of churches.
What discipline is for, and how a case is tried.
How a higher court looks at a lower court, and the four ways a matter goes up.
The Directory for Worship, and which parts of it carry the force of law.
How the Constitution is amended, what changed lately, and how other Presbyterian bodies differ.

alerts.h: Printing the Book of Church Order word for word needs permission
alerts.p: The 2026 edition carries a notice against reproducing its text, and it names electronic resources and AI models in particular. Every provision in this course is therefore put in other words and cited, and none of the wording is reproduced. That includes the ordination and membership vows, which lose force in paraphrase.
alerts.fix: If the vows or any section are to be printed or displayed word for word for a class, ask the Office of the Stated Clerk (ac@pcanet.org) in writing first.

alerts.h: Two early dates are in conflict between archives
alerts.p: The PCA Historical Center dates the first American synod to 1717. The Presbyterian Historical Society dates its creation to 1716. Sources also differ on the year the Old Side and New Side divided.
alerts.fix: Both dates are shown in the history lesson. Settle them against a printed history before teaching them as fixed.

alerts.h: One 2026 change cannot be shown as a redline
alerts.p: The 2026 edition marks a changed line in BCO 18-2 but does not print the former wording, so what the sentence used to say is not recoverable from this edition.
alerts.fix: Compare with the 2025 edition or the Assembly minutes if the exact change matters.

alerts.h: Office-holding rules in other denominations were not checked
alerts.p: The comparison lesson holds to points checked in each body’s own documents: property, the councils or courts, and the make-up of the assembly. Who may hold office in the OPC or the PC(USA) was not checked here and is left out.
alerts.fix: Check each body’s own form of government before adding those rows for a class.
